**Analysis:**

The test image shows two bell peppers with very large, dark brown-to-black, sunken lesions with visible concentric ring patterns — advanced stage, likely with coalesced spots. The Anthracnose reference confirms the same host (bell pepper) with circular sunken spots, though the reference is early-stage (smaller, orange-brown center). The test image represents advanced Anthracnose where lesions have expanded, darkened, and merged — consistent with the description: "expand to ½" in diameter, darken progressively, and may merge to cause complete fruit decay" with "concentric ring pattern."

No other class fits as well: Phytophthora Blight describes "leathery, chocolate brown" without prominent rings; Gray Mold shows fluffy gray spores; Bacterial Canker shows small bird-eye spots. Anthracnose is the best match for sunken, dark, concentric-ringed lesions on fruit.
